claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure composed of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated alloy has low room-temperature tensile ductility.
Dislocation pile-ups at sharp lamellar boundaries produce local stress concentrations in the untreated alloy.
The boundary stress concentrations cause microcracking and premature failure.
The proposed intervention is annealing at approximately 700°C for several minutes followed immediately by rapid quenching.
The proposed annealing and quenching treatment will form an ultrathin interfacial precipitate or interphase along the lamellar boundaries.
The treatment-induced interfacial phase will be coherent and ductile.
The interfacial phase will act as a dislocation sink.
The interfacial phase will absorb and deflect dislocations, thereby reducing dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries.
Deformation of a coherent lamellar interfacial structure can alleviate local stress concentration rather than create a crack.
Reducing interfacial pile-ups and stress concentrations will mitigate microcrack initiation during straining.
The treated alloy will have higher room-temperature strain-to-failure than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will maintain or increase tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
Successful treatment requires precise control of annealing temperature and duration so that a continuous coherent interfacial phase forms without coarsening the lamellar microstructure.
Departures from the processing window may prevent interfacial-phase formation or degrade the lamellar architecture.
